episode.title: The Real Reason The Eiffel Tower Still Stands!

synopsis: The Eiffel Tower was originally intended for demolition after its 20-year permit expired, but its use as a radio antenna secured its permanent survival by 1909.
narration: The Eiffel Tower was designed for demolition after its 20-year permit. However, by 1909, its strategic value as a long-distance radio antenna made it indispensable. This innovative communication technology ultimately saved the iconic landmark from being dismantled.

shots.prompt: A dramatic, low-angle wide shot of the Eiffel Tower's base, looking up through its intricate iron lattice. Early 20th-century Parisian men and women in period attire stroll below, some glancing up with a sense of awe and contemplation under a slightly overcast sky.

A dynamic, upward-looking close-up shot of the Eiffel Tower's upper sections, focusing on newly installed, intricate radio antenna wires and insulators against a vibrant clear blue sky. Birds fly past, emphasizing the height and scale.

music: A majestic, driving orchestral score featuring prominent brass and soaring strings, underpinned by a persistent, dramatic percussive beat. It conveys a sense of enduring grandeur and technological triumph, building with an optimistic, resolute energy, ending mid-climax for a strong loop.
